lead.title: Qare, part of HealthHero, wins a three-year renewal of its teleconsultation company approval, the key to reimbursement
lead.deck: Since France's 2023 social security financing act (LFSS), national health insurance only reimburses teleconsultations by doctors employed by specialist companies if those companies are approved; Qare's first approval, granted in April 2024 for two years, expired in April 2026, and the renewal conditions were only published in July. Caught up in the row over "queue-jumping fees", which the ministry threatened in September to punish by withdrawing approval, the platform brought itself into compliance and secures its reimbursed model until around 2029, while other players reliant on such fees remain under pressure.

milestone.title: After Silicon Practice's collapse, NHS England reviews its procurement frameworks to tighten resilience requirements for GP digital suppliers
milestone.summary: The Swindon supplier, which served more than 470 GP practices (websites, chatbots, the FootFall online consultation platform), went into administration in October. Health minister Dame Diana Johnson told Parliament that NHS England is reviewing its procurement frameworks to widen the choice of tools and tighten checks on supplier standards, resilience and business continuity.
milestone.why: The bar for primary care vendors is shifting: financial strength and continuity plans will weigh more, favouring well-capitalised players and pushing young companies to prove their resilience before signing practices.

brefsEurope.title: SleepCogni rolls out 100 devices for paediatric insomnia at Sheffield Children's NHS Foundation Trust
brefsEurope.summary: Funded by the NIHR and Innovate UK, the rollout lets children on the sleep service waiting list, or referred from the community, use the device at home for up to three months to self-manage their sleep; an independent health economic assessment will be run by the Centre for Healthcare Equipment and Technology Adoption.

brefsEurope.title: Resah's pooled purchases of digital systems top €1 billion in 2025
brefsEurope.summary: According to its annual report, the French purchasing body ordered €1.019B of digital systems in 2025, about 30% of its €3.4B total (up from 21% in 2023), making it the fastest-growing category, ahead of medical devices and medicines. A must-have distribution channel for vendors targeting French hospitals.

brefsIntl.title: Dyania Health teams up with NVIDIA to run its clinical reasoning AI inside hospital firewalls
brefsIntl.summary: Synapsis AI reads the full patient record on the hospital's own infrastructure; at Cleveland Clinic, the first named customer, it answered 88 clinical questions for each of 7,812 aortic valve replacement patients (2005-2021) to estimate valve failure risk. An on-premise "sovereign AI" model that echoes European data-localisation demands.

brefsIntl.title: Mayo Clinic Platform embeds AI decision support covering 35+ specialties into the EHR
brefsIntl.summary: The tool combines a clinical chat (differential diagnoses, treatment options) with 22 clinical calculators, available from November 2026 to Mayo clinicians and organisations in its provider programmes; the announcement gives no figures on accuracy or time saved.

word.definition: A consultation where patient and doctor are not in the same room and talk by video, from a smartphone, a computer or a booth in a pharmacy, ending with a prescription and, under conditions, reimbursement.

parts.label: Access point
parts.role: app, website or teleconsultation kiosk/booth at a partner pharmacy or optician

parts.label: Doctor network
parts.role: clinicians, sometimes employed by the teleconsultation company, available without appointment over long hours

parts.label: Reimbursement framework
parts.role: in France, the company's ministerial approval is the condition for reimbursing consultations by its salaried doctors

how.t: The patient connects online or from a device in a pharmacy; at MEDADOM, a GP is available without appointment 7 days a week, 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.
The doctor runs the visit by video; assisted booths add measuring equipment and maintenance, which the operator has to fund.
The visit is billed to national health insurance if the company is approved: approval is renewed for three years, on an application filed at least four months before it expires.

word.why: Regulation is sorting the French market: since the 2023 LFSS, no approval means no reimbursement, and in September 2026 the ministry threatened to withdraw approval from platforms charging "queue-jumping fees". Usage is growing (15% of adults had at least one teleconsultation in 2024, per DREES) but does not guarantee profitability, as Tessan's receivership shows: value is shifting to approved, compliant players able to fund their kiosk and doctor networks.

startups.name: MEDADOM
startups.use: Online and pharmacy-kiosk teleconsultation; first company to win a three-year renewal of its approval, with founders back in majority control alongside Verdane and Bpifrance

startups.name: Kry
startups.use: Swedish online and in-clinic primary care platform, which bought rival Min Doktor in November 2026 to expand its clinic network

startups.name: Tessan
startups.use: Assisted teleconsultation booths at 1,700+ partners, placed in receivership in April 2026 and aiming to exit the procedure in the autumn
